# Research: non-intrusive-ad-formats

*Auto-generated by AIDLC planning session*

**Question:** If light ads are introduced later, what ad formats are considered least disruptive in focus-oriented utility apps? Are there ad networks that specialize in sports or betting-adjacent content that meet reasonable quality bars?

---

# Non-Intrusive Ad Formats for Focus-Oriented Utility Apps

## Context & Framing

Scroll-down appears to be a sports utility app where the core UX is speed and focus — users want to check scores, lines, or stats quickly and leave. This creates a specific constraint: ads must not interrupt task completion or add cognitive load to the lookup flow. The research below covers formats, networks, and implementation considerations tailored to that context.

---

## 1. Ad Format Taxonomy: Least-to-Most Disruptive

### Tier 1 — Near-Invisible (Recommended Starting Point)

#### 1a. Native List Item Ads
Rendered as a row in an existing list (e.g., between game cards), using the same visual language as content. A subtle "Sponsored" label is required for compliance, but the row doesn't break scroll rhythm.

- **Best fit:** Feed-style interfaces where games are listed vertically
- **User tolerance:** High — feels like content unless overstyled
- **Implementation note:** Must match font, spacing, and card elevation exactly. Deviation is what triggers "ad blindness" plus annoyance.
- **Example label:** Small gray "Ad" badge in the top-right corner of the card, same position as a status chip

#### 1b. Inline Banner Below Fold (Sticky-Free)
A static banner that lives at a natural scroll stop — the bottom of a completed section, not fixed to the viewport. Does not follow the user.

- **Best fit:** After a completed game card group or at end of a scrollable list
- **Size:** 320×50 or 300×100 — small enough to not consume focus real estate
- **What to avoid:** `position: fixed` or `position: sticky` — any motion-linked placement competes with the content scan

#### 1c. Sponsorship Attribution Lines
A single text line ("Today's odds powered by [Sponsor]") attached to an existing UI element rather than a standalone ad unit. Common in sports apps.

- **Revenue model:** Typically CPM or flat weekly sponsorship deals
- **Regulatory note:** In betting-adjacent apps, this phrasing can trigger sportsbook advertising rules depending on jurisdiction — needs legal review per market

---

### Tier 2 — Moderate (Acceptable with Care)

#### 2a. Interstitial at Natural Transition Points
Full-screen or large modal ads shown only at deliberate navigation transitions — e.g., when a user taps from the main feed into a game detail view, the ad fires before the destination loads.

- **Timing:** Max 1 per session, not per navigation event
- **Skip behavior:** Must offer a visible close target within 3 seconds (5 seconds is the outer limit before bounce rates spike)
- **IAB standard:** IAB "Rising Stars" interstitials with mandatory close button

#### 2b. Rewarded Opt-In Ads (Video)
User explicitly taps "Watch a short ad for [benefit]" — e.g., to unlock a premium stat view, remove ads for an hour, or get a free pick.

- **User tolerance:** Very high when value exchange is real and immediate
- **Completion rates:** Industry average 70–85% for rewarded video vs. ~1% for banner CTR
- **Downside:** Requires designing a reward system, which is non-trivial

#### 2c. End-of-Session Notification-Style Prompts
After the user's natural session end (app backgrounded or navigated away), a push notification-style ad surfaces. Not technically an in-app ad, but relevant for monetization without interrupting active use.

---

### Tier 3 — High Disruption (Avoid in V1)

- Auto-play video with sound
- Interstitials between every tap
- Ads that resize content or cause layout shift (CLS-inducing)
- Overlays that cover the primary content without a clear close path
- Any ad that blocks navigation (back button capture)

---

## 2. Ad Networks with Sports/Betting-Adjacent Inventory

### Tier A — Established, Policy-Safe

#### Google AdMob / AdSense
- **URL:** admob.google.com
- **Sports inventory:** Moderate — contextual targeting can surface sportsbook, sports gear, fantasy sports ads
- **Betting policy:** AdMob permits licensed gambling ads in jurisdictions where it's legal; requires account-level policy attestation and geo-targeting
- **Fill rates:** High globally (>95% in US/EU)
- **eCPM range (sports):** $1–$6 CPM for banner; $8–$25 CPM for interstitial; $15–$40 CPM for rewarded video (US)
- **Integration:** React Native via `react-native-google-mobile-ads`; Web via standard AdSense tag
- **Minimum payout:** $100, monthly via wire or check

#### Meta Audience Network
- **URL:** audiencenetwork.com
- **Sports inventory:** Strong — Meta's behavioral targeting surfaces fantasy, sportsbook, and sports retail at above-average relevance
- **Betting policy:** Same licensed-operator requirement; geo-restriction tools available
- **eCPM range:** Competitive with AdMob; often 20–40% higher on rewarded video
- **Integration:** React Native via `react-native-fbads` (community-maintained); declining support, check SDK status before committing
- **Note:** Meta AAN has been winding down for some publishers — verify current availability at time of integration

---

### Tier B — Sports-Specific or Betting-Adjacent Specialists

#### Playwire
- **URL:** playwire.com
- **Specialty:** Publisher-side revenue platform with sports media focus; works with Bleacher Report, SB Nation alumni publishers
- **Model:** Managed service — they handle ad ops, you share ~30% of revenue
- **Inventory quality:** Premium direct-sold sports brand deals mixed with programmatic
- **Minimum traffic requirement:** ~500K monthly pageviews or sessions to qualify
- **Best for:** Mid-to-large publishers wanting hands-off monetization

#### Minute Media / 90min Ad Network
- **URL:** minutemedia.com
- **Specialty:** Direct sports content and advertising network; runs ads across their owned sports properties and partner sites
- **Model:** Programmatic + direct; CPM-based
- **Contact:** Publisher partnerships team; no public self-serve portal
- **Best for:** If you have a sports-specific content angle and want brand-aligned inventory

#### BetMakers / Amelco (Betting Data + Ads Hybrid)
- Not traditional ad networks — they supply real-time odds data that can be wrapped in affiliate/advertising revenue models
- More relevant if you're building odds-display features where the data itself is the ad unit (e.g., clicking odds links to a sportsbook via affiliate deep link)

---

### Tier C — Affiliate-Based (High CPM Alternative)

Rather than traditional display ads, affiliate placements with sportsbooks can dramatically outperform banner eCPM:

#### Bet365 Affiliates
- **URL:** bet365affiliates.com
- **Model:** Revenue share (25–35% of net gaming revenue from referred users) or CPA ($50–$200 per depositing player)
- **Compliance:** Age-gating and responsible gambling disclosures required; jurisdictional restrictions apply

#### DraftKings / FanDuel Affiliate Programs
- Both run through in-house affiliate programs
- **DraftKings:** draftkings.com/affiliates
- **FanDuel:** fanduel.com/affiliates
- **CPA rates:** $50–$150 per first deposit (varies by sport season and acquisition campaigns)
- **Best format:** Native card with odds + CTA ("Bet this game on DraftKings") — functions as both content and ad
- **Revenue potential:** A single converted user can be worth 10x a thousand banner impressions

#### PointsBet / ESPN Bet
- Newer entrant programs with higher CPA rates to gain market share
- Worth monitoring — aggressive acquisition budgets in 2024–2026 window

---

## 3. Technical Implementation Considerations

### Avoiding Layout Shift (CLS)
The single biggest UX sin in focus apps is content jumping when an ad loads. Mitigations:

```css
/* Reserve space before ad loads */
.ad-slot {
  min-height: 50px; /* match your expected banner height */
  background: transparent;
}
```

Or in React Native, use a placeholder with fixed dimensions:

```jsx
<View style={{ height: 50, width: '100%' }} />
{adLoaded && <AdComponent />}
```

### Frequency Capping
Most SDKs support this natively but defaults are aggressive. Recommended caps for a utility app:
- Banner: 1 refresh per 60 seconds (default is often 30)
- Interstitial: 1 per session (default is often per-navigation)
- Rewarded: Uncapped (user-initiated)

### Ad-Free Premium Toggle
If you ever offer a paid tier, the infrastructure for suppressing ads cleanly matters. Pattern:

```js
// Check subscription status before rendering ad slot
const { isPremium } = useSubscription();
if (isPremium) return null;
return <AdBanner />;
```

### GDPR / CCPA Consent
Required for any network operating in EU or California. AdMob and Meta both have consent management SDKs. Skipping this is the most common compliance miss for small publishers:
- **AdMob UMP SDK:** Google's User Messaging Platform handles consent flows
- **Avoid:** Building your own consent dialog — use the network's SDK to stay in compliance as regulations evolve

## 4. Revenue Benchmarks (US Sports App Context)

| Format | Typical eCPM (US) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Banner 320×50 | $0.50–$2.00 | Low but passive |
| Banner 300×250 | $1.50–$5.00 | Better visual real estate |
| Interstitial | $5–$20 | Session-limited |
| Rewarded Video | $15–$50 | Best RPM, requires UX design |
| Native Feed Ad | $2–$8 | Varies by relevance match |
| Sportsbook Affiliate CPA | $50–$200/user | Non-recurring but high value |
| Sportsbook Revenue Share | 25–35% lifetime NGR | Long-tail, unpredictable |

---

## 5. Recommended Phased Approach

### Phase 1 — Validate Tolerance (No Revenue Pressure)
Introduce one native list item ad per 10 game cards, using AdMob house ads (free, internal) pointing to your own app features. Measure session length change and scroll depth to establish a baseline before any real ads appear.

### Phase 2 — Low-Density Programmatic
Enable AdMob or Playwire with frequency caps set conservatively. Single banner placement, below-fold, non-sticky. Monitor session length, bounce rate, and App Store reviews for sentiment signals.

### Phase 3 — Affiliate Integration
Add one affiliate CTA card per sport session (e.g., "Live lines on DraftKings" inline with the game card that has odds). This is higher value and potentially more useful to the user than generic display ads.

### Phase 4 — Rewarded (If Warranted)
Only introduce rewarded video if you have a concrete value exchange to offer. Without that, rewarded ads feel manipulative rather than optional.

---

## 6. Quality Bar Checklist

Before enabling any ad network or format, verify:

- [ ] Ads do not autoplay audio without user interaction
- [ ] Close/dismiss target is ≥ 44×44pt tap target
- [ ] No layout shift on ad load (CLS score < 0.1)
- [ ] Frequency cap set at session level for interstitials
- [ ] Consent flow implemented for EU/CA users
- [ ] Gambling ads geo-restricted to licensed jurisdictions
- [ ] Age gate or responsible gambling disclosure present if sportsbook ads are enabled
- [ ] Ad slots have fixed dimensions reserved before load
- [ ] No back-button capture by ad overlay
